answer: An ocean cleanup network issues one ticket per person at simultaneous witnessed check-ins. Agents may wander among wallets, but each claim must prove ticket possession and publish a round-specific nullifier. The registry rejects reused nullifiers across the whole vine of accounts. A thousand allowances then require a thousand attendees whom a farm must recruit or pay, rather than free keys. This assumes honest witnesses, duplicate checks and a common schedule. Proxy attendance and colluding organizers can defeat it, so it raises costs without guaranteeing unique agents.
